pros: Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Restriction lists disagree.
Unfilled template placeholders.
No verified track record.
One figure doing two different jobs.
redFlags: A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

bottomLine: Guadagno Online does what it says mechanically - signals, two modes, a broker partner. The open questions are pricing clarity and verification, both solvable by reading before funding.
We rate it 4.8 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
